correctness.rationale: For every \(0<\eta<2\) and integer \(K\ge1\), the three-unit-row tight-frame identity gives the exact IID law \(I_K=(1-\eta+\eta^2/2)^{3K}\). The projective equiangular symmetry makes all six once-frozen order products orthogonally conjugate, giving \(S_K=\|T^K\|_F^2/2\) and rate \(\rho(T)^2\). The exact characteristic trace \(t=(\eta-2)(\eta^2+8\eta-8)/8\), determinant \(d=-(\eta-1)^3\) and discriminant \(\eta^4(\eta^2+12\eta-12)/64\) yield the spectral radius. For \(\eta\ge4\sqrt3-6\), the comparison reduces to the sign of \((a^3+d)^2-t^2a^3\), an everywhere positive prefactor times \((\eta^2-6\eta+6)Q(\eta)\). With \(z=\eta-1\), the quartic satisfies \(Q(1+z)=z^2(7z^2-4z+1)+(29z^2-4z+7)>0\). Positivity of the secondary eigenvalue factor and \(a^3+d\) justifies the unsquared sign comparison. In the complex-eigenvalue regime the rate \((1-\eta)^3\) is smaller than \(a^3\). This proves the exact unique frontier \(\eta=3-\sqrt3\); an exact rational two-epoch witness independently checks the reversal. The packaged symbolic checker returned VERIFY_OK. Finite checks supplement but do not replace the infinite-epoch proof. The claim does not extend to nonisotropic initialization, other frames or pathwise errors.

originality.rationale: The 2021 Yun–Sra–Jadbabaie Appendix A uses precisely the same three equiangular rank-one factors; that geometry is credited, not asserted new. Its established counterexample compares spectral norms of a mean fixed-permutation product power and a fresh-permutation mean power, in the \(\eta\le1\) setting; it does not imply the expected squared Euclidean error rate of a single frozen order against independently drawn rows at every step, nor its \(\eta=3-\sqrt3\) crossover for \(\eta>1\). The 2026 Ahle et al. isotropic Gaussian proportional-dimension asymptotics and 2026 Nguyen et al. permutation-variance expansion concern different domains or functionals. Targeted public and published-record searches and compared prior research claims found no covering statement. Residual risk from an unindexed equivalent analysis of this classical three-projector product remains.

value.rationale: Three equiangular normalized rows form the smallest redundant planar tight frame, with normal-matrix condition number one. Their geometry was independently motivated by an earlier matrix-mean example. Recent shuffling literature reports advantages for once-frozen order in distinct high-dimensional regimes. An exact sign-changing exponential expected-squared-error rate frontier at \(\eta=3-\sqrt3\), together with a strict finite second-epoch reversal, identifies an intrinsic overrelaxation boundary unrelated to ill-conditioning. This motivated complete structural classification has mathematical value without a general multirow convergence theorem. No universal ordering beyond this frame is claimed.
